primitives.name: Global Temperature Scaling
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - Global TS baseline: Q̂i(x,T) = max_l σ_SM(zi(x)/T)(l), T fit by NLL on val (3.3).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'scalar temperature parameter in \\mathbb{R}^+', 'z_i(x)': 'logit vector at location x in \\mathbb{R}^{|L|}', 'σ_SM': 'softmax function'}
primitives.assumptions: Logits follow a multinomial distribution; temperature is constant across space.

primitives.name: Local Temperature Scaling
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **LTS (local TS):** per-pixel/voxel temperature Ti(x) ∈ R+ predicted by network H(α, zi, Ii, x) from the logit map + image: Q̂i(x, Ti(x)) = max_l σ_SM(zi(x)/Ti(x))(l) (3.6).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T_i(x)': 'spatially varying temperature at pixel/voxel x in \\mathbb{R}^+', 'H': 'neural network mapping logits and image to local temperature', 'z_i(x)': 'logit vector at location x in \\mathbb{R}^{|L|}', 'I_i': 'input image tensor'}
primitives.assumptions: Spatial context influences calibration; network learns spatial temperature fields.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When global calibration fails due to localized overconfidence or underconfidence.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphically extends global TS to spatially adaptive calibration via learned temperature fields.
layer2.telemetry: Segmentation accuracy, ECE, SCE, ACE across boundary/local regions.

primitives.name: Contextual Temperature Field
primitives.verbatim_quote: Ti(x) > 1 damps overconfidence; Ti(x) < 1 boosts underconfidence; Ti(x)→∞ → uniform 1/|L|.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T_i(x)': 'contextual temperature field at spatial point x'}
primitives.assumptions: Temperature field encodes spatial calibration behavior; boundedness ensures stability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When temperature approaches infinity or zero, leading to uniform or degenerate predictions.

layer2.mapping: Derives contextual calibration signals from input features to modulate softmax logits.
layer2.telemetry: Reliability diagrams, ECE, and classification consistency metrics.

The core innovation lies in extending temperature scaling from scalar to spatially varying parameters. The global method assumes uniform miscalibration, whereas LTS adapts per-pixel or voxel. This allows for nuanced handling of spatially heterogeneous prediction errors. The neural network H learns a mapping from logits and image features to local temperatures, enabling dynamic adjustment of confidence levels. The softmax operation remains invariant to class ordering, ensuring segmentation accuracy is preserved. Theoretically, this is grounded in information theory where entropy minimization aligns with better-calibrated posteriors. Empirically, LTS outperforms global TS in reducing ECE across multiple domains, especially near object boundaries. The failure mode occurs when the learned temperature field becomes constant, reverting to global TS. This is mitigated by requiring statistical significance in performance gains over global TS.
